answers.answer: Reveal the top region card and put the King in that region. Each player takes another region card as their home region and puts their Grande there. Each player’s initial ten Caballeros are distributed as two beside the Grande in the home region, one on the first success-track space, and seven in that player’s court.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘reveal the top card and put the King in that region’; ‘another region card to determine their home region’; ‘two in their home region beside the Grande, one on the first space ... and seven in their court.’

answers.answer: In round 1, players choose who begins playing power cards. In later rounds, the player who took the last turn in the preceding round starts. Other players play clockwise. A value already played that round may not be matched.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Players choose who begins playing power cards in round 1’; later ‘the player who took the last turn in the preceding round begins’; others play ‘clockwise’; ‘No value already played this round may be matched.’

answers.answer: Turns are taken in descending power-card value. At the start of a turn, recruit up to the Caballero allowance pictured on the power card from the provinces into your court. Recruitment happens before choosing an available face-up action card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Take turns in descending power-card value’; ‘At the start of your turn recruit up to ... from the provinces into your court’; ‘After recruitment, choose an available face-up action card.’

answers.answer: If your provinces do not have enough of your Caballeros, you may take your own pieces from the board to make up the shortfall. The King’s region and the Castillo cannot supply pieces for recruitment.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘If there are insufficient Caballeros of your color in the provinces, you may take your own from the board to make up the difference. The King's region remains taboo and the Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.’

answers.answer: Ordinary deployment moves Caballeros from your court to any regions adjacent to the King’s current region and/or to the Castillo; the allowance may be divided freely among those destinations. It is not required to use the full allowance: the card number is a maximum, and you may deploy fewer, including none.
answers.evidence: Actions: ‘number is a maximum: you may deploy fewer, including none’; ‘from your court to any regions adjacent to the King's current region and/or the Castillo, dividing the allowance freely.’

answers.answer: Ordinary deployment and the special action may be done in either order. Each activity must be completed before starting the other; neither may be split or interleaved. The special action may be declined.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Do them in either order, but complete one activity before starting the other: neither may be split or interleaved. You may decline the special action.’

answers.answer: After a player’s turn, that player lays aside the selected action card, making it unavailable to later players. After all players have taken turns, discard any remaining face-up action cards. The King card is revealed again every round and is never permanently discarded.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Lay aside the selected action card after your turn; later players cannot choose it’; discard remaining face-up cards after everyone has taken a turn; ‘The King card is revealed again every round and never permanently discarded.’

answers.answer: No Caballero, Grande, or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of the King’s region; special actions do not override this taboo. The region may still be scored. Moving the King changes which region is protected.
answers.evidence: Actions—Ordinary deployment and protected locations: ‘no Caballero, Grande or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of it’; ‘It may still be scored’; ‘Actions that move the King are the exception: moving the King changes which region is protected.’

answers.answer: Clearly announce how many Caballeros are being put into the Castillo. The King’s location does not restrict entry into the Castillo. Caballeros cannot be removed from the Castillo by an action; they leave only during general scoring.
answers.evidence: Actions—Ordinary deployment and protected locations: ‘any or all may go into the Castillo, regardless of the King's location. Announce clearly how many you put inside’; ‘No action removes Caballeros from the Castillo; they leave only during general scoring.’

answers.answer: General scoring occurs after rounds 3, 6, and 9. In order: (1) before uncovering the Castillo, every player secretly chooses one board region other than the King’s region for all of that player’s Castillo Caballeros and places the disk face down; (2) uncover and score the Castillo; (3) reveal disks and move each player’s Castillo Caballeros to the chosen region, except pieces chosen for the King’s region go to that player’s court, then replace the Castillo empty; (4) score the nine regions in scoring-track order and record points. Thus destinations are selected secretly before the Castillo is uncovered.
answers.evidence: General scoring after rounds 3, 6 and 9; stage 1 says ‘Secretly select destinations before uncovering the Castillo’; stages 2–4 specify score Castillo, reveal and empty it, then score the nine regions in track order.

answers.answer: A player may not split their Castillo Caballeros: all must go to one destination. The destination may not be the King’s region, because the secret selection rule excludes it. Pieces cannot be kept in the Castillo; it is emptied after scoring. If a player selected the King’s region, those pieces go to that player’s court instead.
answers.evidence: General scoring: select ‘any board region except the King's region’ and ‘All that player's Castillo Caballeros must go to one region’; then move every player's pieces to the selected region, with King’s-region selection sending them to court; ‘Replace the Castillo empty.’

answers.answer: The three players tied at four Caballeros each score 3 points apiece (the second-place value); the player with three Caballeros scores 1 point (third place). Grandes do not count toward majority; only Caballeros count.
answers.evidence: Region ranks: ‘A Grande marks a home region and contributes zero Caballeros’; example on 5/3/1: counts ‘4,4,4,3’ score ‘3,3,3,1.’

answers.answer: The player with 4 scores 6 points, the player with 3 scores 4 points, and both players with 2 score 0 points each.
answers.evidence: Region ranks example on 6/4/2: counts ‘4,3,2,2’ score ‘6,4,0,0.’

answers.answer: In a two-player game, only first place can pay. In a three-player game, only first and second can pay. A two-player tie for first shifts to the next rank, which is not payable in a two-player game, so neither player scores.
answers.evidence: Region ranks: ‘Two players: only first place can pay. Three players: only first and second can pay’; ‘a two-player tie for first pays neither player.’

answers.answer: Whenever the relevant region is scored, including during special scoring, the sole majority holder in the King’s region gets a +2 King’s bonus, and the sole majority holder who has their own Grande in that region gets a +2 home bonus. Neither bonus is awarded on a tie for first.
answers.evidence: Bonuses apply ‘whenever the relevant region is scored, including special scorings’; King’s bonus +2 for the ‘sole majority holder’; Home bonus +2 if the ‘sole majority holder has their own Grande’; neither is awarded on a tie for first.

answers.answer: Special scoring of the Castillo reveals and scores its contents, then covers the same Caballeros again. It does not empty or redistribute them; redistribution waits for general scoring.
answers.evidence: Actions—Ordinary deployment: ‘Special scoring of the Castillo reveals and scores its contents, then covers them again without redistribution’; Stack 3 says cover ‘the same Caballeros’ and redistribution waits until general scoring.

answers.answer: A mobile scoreboard may be placed at the Castillo. It may not move into or out of the King’s region, the two mobile scoreboards may not be stacked, and they must stay right side up as 8/4/0 or 4/0/0; they cannot be rotated to invent other values.
answers.evidence: Stack 4—Mobile scoreboard: ‘Castillo is allowed’; ‘No movement into or out of the King's region’; scoreboards ‘cannot be stacked’; place right side up as 8/4/0 or 4/0/0, ‘never reversed or rotated to invent other values.’

answers.answer: Move your Grande to another region other than the King’s region or the Castillo. It cannot leave the King’s region. A destination may already contain several Grandes. After moving, the destination becomes your new home region.
answers.evidence: Stack 4—Grande: ‘Move your Grande to another region except the King's region or Castillo. It cannot leave the King's region. A destination may already contain several Grandes. The destination becomes your new home region.’

answers.answer: The recovery action may return any one of your played power cards to your hand, including the card played this turn. You do not need to reveal which card you choose, although taking the visible top card will be apparent.
answers.evidence: Stack 4—Power Cards: ‘Return any one of your played power cards to hand, including the one played this turn. You need not reveal which; taking the visible top card will of course be apparent.’

answers.answer: The game ends after all stages of the third general scoring, after round 9. The winner is whoever is furthest along the success track; no additional endgame tiebreaker is given.
answers.evidence: End: ‘Finish all stages of the third general scoring, after round 9. Whoever is furthest along the success track wins. The source gives no additional endgame tiebreaker.’
